scope: Read-only source/result audit of the existing Dart CEL candidate; not a package adoption decision or production conformance claim

package.name: cel
package.observedRuntime: Dart 3.11.1 VM, macOS arm64 (from existing T1 result)
package.dependencyNote: pubspec.lock pins cel 0.6.1 and its transitive packages; Dart result is from the installed source path above. No new install or execution was performed.

results.resultFormatCaveat: probe.dart maps thrown exceptions to {type:error}; matching error rows do not identify the failure reason. In particular dart/C18 matches the expected error only because timestamp() is unsupported, so it does not demonstrate rejection of an invalid calendar date.

mismatchFindings.finding: The library delegates double + int to Dart's dynamic numeric addition and returns DoubleValue; this is not a result-encoding mismatch. The fixture expects CEL's same-type double overload rather than mixed double/int promotion.
IntValue.add has no signed 64-bit overflow check; the existing VM result wraps to the minimum signed int. Probe encoding faithfully labels that Dart int as int.

StandardLibrary explicitly leaves macros unimplemented. has is a macro requiring AST-level presence semantics; the current planner instead reports an unsupported unary function. This is not the adapter's error mapping creating the mismatch.

The library documents macros as unsupported. The planner accepts only one- or two-operand function calls; comprehension macro expansion for filter/map is absent. The captured UnsupportedError comes from that runtime limitation.
The package explicitly says timestamp protos are unsupported and comments TimestampType out of its type registry. No timezone-aware timestamp receiver/getHours implementation is present.
The package README lists type as unsupported; the planner has no type overload and reports a runtime UnsupportedError. The error is not an adapter classification.

visitUint strips the suffix and constructs IntLiteralExpr; the AST has no uint literal node. encode then observes the returned Dart int. This is an upstream value-model loss, not a formatter-only mistake.

nonMismatchCaveat.finding: The invalid date expression errors because timestamp() is not implemented, not because 2026-02-30 was parsed and rejected. Count it as a coincidental shape match only; malformed-date validation remains untested.

implementationGaps.neededWork: Preserve int/double/uint distinctions and the signed CEL int range; add missing type and has semantics and standard filter/map macro expansion; rerun the shared 22 fixtures.

implementationGaps.priority: required by the current CEL contract
implementationGaps.neededWork: The probe parses, plans and evaluates each fixture; it contains no Dart registration or static type-check experiment. Environment.compile is parser-only, makeProgram wraps the expression in CheckedExpression without checking it, and the environment's declarations are not used by the planner. Add a real non-evaluating checker that rejects undeclared variables/functions and invalid overloads at registration. Syntax errors can still be caught during parsing; the gap is semantic checking.

There is no evaluation budget, operation-cost counter or cancellation/decorator hook; Program.evaluate is synchronous. matches directly calls Dart RegExp.hasMatch, with no RE2 conformance or per-match bound. Implement and verify the contract's non-recoverable evaluation budget and RE2-compatible, bounded regex path; the synchronous call cannot be interrupted from the same isolate. A Worker/isolate deadline alone would not establish cost accounting.

implementationGaps.priority: required for date CEL support; currently absent
implementationGaps.neededWork: Implement strict CEL timestamp parsing/representation and the required receiver getters at the runtime type/provider and standard-library function paths. Validate actual calendar date, offset, milliseconds, range, and timezone semantics; timestamp() must not bypass the strict parser. Date/timezone helper package/API viability and Dart VM versus Flutter/web parity were not tested here.

The package's public barrel exports only Ast, Environment and Program. The observed custom function/type plumbing relies on package:cel/src internals and there is no public Environment constructor/options API in this version. Confirm whether the required patches are maintained as a fork or whether upstream exposes a stable extension API before relying on these hooks.

conclusion.basis: Seven of 22 shared CEL fixtures mismatch for package-level semantics or missing functions/types. Static semantic checking, cost limits, bounded RE2 semantics, and strict timestamp support are also absent from the inspected 0.6.1 source. The existing Node worker deadline, JS/calendar experiments, and adapters do not verify these Dart capabilities.
uncertainties: No Dart/browser/Flutter execution or new package run was performed; the evidence is the existing Dart 3.11.1 VM result and installed source inspection.
Runtime behavior outside the recorded macOS arm64 Dart VM, particularly Dart web integer representation, regular-expression behavior, and timezone database parity, remains unverified.
The mismatch list is the seven rows marked mismatches in existing T1 results; error-row details are probe-caught Dart exceptions and do not establish compatible error codes or all edge cases.
